item.title: One of Hilma af Klint's Amazingly Rare Abstract Paintings Sold for a Record $12.7 Million at Auction. But Should It Have Been on Sale at All?
item.description: After "Ser III No. 5," painted in 1920, sold for nearly 16 times its pre-sale estimate, critics charged that af Klint wanted to keep her "holy body of work" together in a temple, not spread across private collections

item.title: The Search for a Top Dark Matter Candidate Was Losing Hope. Then Came a Potential Signal. Will It Be Enough to Energize the Struggling Field?
item.description: Physicists were growing weary with WIMPs, one proposed contender for the particles that make up dark matter. Despite their new cautious optimism, many challenges remain

item.title: A Roman Cup and Hundreds of Other Treasures Unearthed in This 2,000-Year-Old Tomb Reveal the Rich Exchange Network of an Ancient Asian Empire
item.description: The Xiongnu people dominated Central Asia for some 300 years. Now, a grave discovered in Mongolia has revealed the pastoral culture’s links to the Roman Empire, Han China and the Lelang Commandery

item.title: Rembrandt's 'Night Watch' Is Teeming With Life. Researchers Reveal a Hidden World of Microbes All Over the Masterpiece
item.description: Samples swabbed from the 17th-century painting reveal myriad microorganisms, including one perplexing bacterium that was first discovered at a Japanese sugar refinery in 2013

item.title: For the First Time, Astronomers Witnessed a Giant Star Gobble Up Its Smaller Stellar Companion
item.description: The merger caused an eruption in late 2025, which researchers rushed to document using several ground- and space-based telescopes. With older data and the help of computer simulations, the team reconstructed the entire astrophysical process

item.title: An Isolated Group of Amazonian Hunter-Gatherers Made a Rare Request for Help From Outsiders, Raising Concerns About Forest Degradation
item.description: Around 20 members of the Indigenous Awá tribe emerged from the rainforest and received food from neighboring villagers. The group has not made contact with the outside world in decades, so experts say deforestation may have left these individuals with no other option

item.title: Nine-Pound Eagles Seem to Be Hunting 60-Pound Baboons in Africa—Hinting the Predators May Have Gone After Our Ancestors, Too
item.description: In northeastern Chad, researchers found evidence of Verreaux's eagles attacking full-grown olive baboons weighing as much as a small human. The findings suggest early hominins had to watch out for ambushes from the sky, which may have shaped their evolution

item.title: Dutch Elm Disease Virtually Wiped Out America's Most Iconic Tree. Now, Scientists Are Engineering a Comeback for the Beloved Species
item.description: Researchers are working to restore the American elm to the natural landscape—and eventually your front yard

item.title: Teeth Discovered in Two Chinese Caves Are Rewriting the Story of Homo Erectus, an Ancient Human Ancestor That May Have Been More Capable Than We Thought
item.description: One new study suggests that the species persisted in mainland Asia for 216,000 years longer than previously thought. Another says Homo erectus was capable of living in a tropical rainforest, a discovery that turns a common extinction theory "on its head," according to one researcher

item.title: In Peacock's 'Dig,' Amy Poehler Plays an Archaeologist Who Discovers an Extraordinary Statue in Greece. What Do Real Experts Think of the TV Series?
item.description: Co-created by Michael Schur, the show is based on Kate Myers' 2023 novel, "Excavations." All ten episodes will be available to stream on November 23
